domain_context.shared_foundations: XR learners need digital/programming and 3D/spatial literacy appropriate to the chosen pathway, user-centered design, interactive-system concepts and an understanding of how runtime, tracking, display and input constrain an experience. The depth is pathway-specific; a content designer does not need the same hardware depth as a platform engineer.
domain_context.nigerian_context: Targeted searches found a Lagos XR developer vacancy (Insightful3d), the Imisi 3D XR lab, OAU animation-lab XR activity, and ABU's reported discussion of a proposed VR learning facility. These are concrete local activity examples, not a national labor-demand or degree/certification claim. No Nigeria-specific device-engineering or human-factors job evidence was identified in this pass.

relationships.explanation: Interaction flows, spatial scenarios, content assets and test criteria specify what the application must render and how users act; implementation and user tests return feasibility/usability evidence to design.
Runtime APIs expose supported sessions, views, input and device-specific features; application feature detection and compatibility tests must respect the actual runtime/platform.
Pose/plane/anchor estimates feed content placement and spatial interaction, with environment quality, permission, tracking error and update latency as constraints.

CloudXR requires a compatible server runtime/application and client SDK pair; network latency, bandwidth and reliability become end-to-end experience constraints. This is an optional architecture, not a universal XR prerequisite.
Task performance, comfort, accessibility, sickness, privacy and adverse-event findings inform redesign and acceptance; evaluation instruments must match the construct and population.
USD and related scene formats support content composition/interchange; target runtime/renderers may not support every asset feature, interaction, material or extension.

source_registry.title: Khronos OpenXR
source_registry.supports: Runtime-facing API for session lifecycle, tracking/input state and rendered-frame submission; supports cross-platform application development.
source_registry.claim_limit: OpenXR standard scope does not make extensions, runtimes, device capabilities or performance identical.

source_registry.title: Khronos OpenXR registry
source_registry.supports: OpenXR 1.1 specifications, API references, SDK and conformance-test resources.
source_registry.claim_limit: Registry documents the interface and conformance suite; passing conformance does not validate an application’s usability or safety.

source_registry.title: W3C WebXR Device API, Candidate Recommendation Draft (9 June 2026)
source_registry.supports: Browser APIs for VR/AR sessions, view/pose, input and rendering; the draft also documents consent, trusted UI and sensitive pose-data protections.
source_registry.claim_limit: This is a Candidate Recommendation Draft with open issues, not a final Recommendation or universal device-availability guarantee.

source_registry.title: IEEE Digital Reality standards portfolio
source_registry.supports: Current project families cover device taxonomy, immersive video/content, immersive UI, environment safety, virtual-object mapping/interoperability, immersive audio and AR learning models.
source_registry.claim_limit: Projects/work items show standards needs and scope; they are not all published standards and do not define a universal career taxonomy.

source_registry.title: IEEE 3079-2020: HMD-Based VR Sickness Reduction Technology
source_registry.supports: Active standard focused on sickness-reduction technology for HMD VR.
source_registry.claim_limit: Narrow standard subject; it does not establish a complete comfort model or guarantee sickness prevention.

source_registry.title: IEEE P7030: Ethical Assessment of XR Technologies
source_registry.supports: Project scope covers socio-technical and ethical assessment of XR systems.
source_registry.claim_limit: Recommended-practice project status must be kept distinct from a published standard or legal requirement.

source_registry.title: W3C XR Accessibility User Requirements
source_registry.supports: User needs for multimodal access, alternative input, motion-agnostic interaction, accessible navigation and immersive content.
source_registry.claim_limit: A Working Group Note, not a conformance standard; requirements depend on user and application context.

source_registry.title: W3C WCAG 3.0 Working Draft
source_registry.supports: Draft provisions address immersive captions, direction cues, orientation, and multimodal accessibility.
source_registry.claim_limit: It remains a Working Draft; do not present draft provisions as current WCAG conformance requirements.

source_registry.supports: Field-of-view, depth, readable content, interaction spacing, indirect gestures and movement-minimizing guidance.
